messages:
sam: dropped a small pass on the prompt-sets -> evals handoff UX. Focused on density controls, approval lifecycle, and undo scope. Can the product/design folks eyeball before I lock the spec?
maria: link to prototype: https://figma.com/file/hand-off-density (WIP)
jess: quick skim  overall looks good. Two immediate things: header language and bulk CTA. We use 'Regressions' in some places and 'Changes' elsewhere. Can we standardize?
liam: prefer neutral top-level: 'Changes'. Reserve 'Regression' as a per-row badge when delta < -threshold. Less scary on dashboards.
ara: accessibility nit: when toggling density (Compact / Cozy), ensure SR users get announced context: "Switched to Compact view" and that the toggle is a real control (aria-pressed or role=tab).
eva: bulk CTA: current label 'Approve selected' is ambiguous. Options: 'Approve runs', 'Approve batch', or just 'Approve'. I vote 'Approve runs' for clarity.
sam: agree on 'Approve runs'. Also propose splitting actions: Run tests (left) and Approve runs (right) to avoid accidental approvals right after a run.
maria: split CTAs sounds safer. We'll also add a small guard: a pre-approve validation that runs quick checks (missing prompt, empty input, test count==0) and surfaces warnings/errors.
jess: for warnings we should show 'Approve anyway' in the modal. For errors block the action and link to fixes. Keep keyboard focus inside modal and ensure aria-labelledby.
liam: undo scope: if someone approves multiple batches, Undo should revert only the last batch (LIFO). Toast copy should be explicit: "Approved 8 runs. Undo last approve (8 runs)". Make Undo tabbable and have aria-label="Undo last approve 8 runs".
ara: compact mode comment behavior: don't fully hide comments. Show a comment dot with count that opens a flyout on enter/space. aria-label="Open comments for <test name>". Flyout should trap focus and be escape-closeable.
eva: visual cues: color alone is not enough for score drops. Add an up/down icon and textual delta like "-0.12". Also legend should have text nodes: 'score up', 'score down'.
ux-bot: Suggestion: add 'Pilot approve' flow for staged rollouts: small subset -> promote. UI notes: present presets (1%, 5%, 10%) + custom, label 'Pilot: 5 runs', and show pilot progress toast with aria-live polite.
sam: we should not call it 'canary' in product UI. Use 'Pilot' or 'Staged rollout'. 'Pilot approve' then 'Promote to all' as second step.
maria: audit trail: every approve (including pilot promotes) creates an audit row with user, counts, and reason (if provided). Undo should mark audit as reverted and persist history.
jess: microcopy: header label 'Changes' and CTA 'Approve runs'. For per-row badges use sentence case: 'Regression', 'Change detected'. Keep consistency with console.
liam: keyboard flow ordering: when tabbing inside a row prefer: chevron (expand) -> comment dot -> checkbox -> actions. That reads as 'review then act'. We'll spec that order.
ara: a11y: when a row expands, announce via aria-live: "Expanded <test name>, score delta -0.07". Also ensure expand respects prefers-reduced-motion.
eva: pre-approve validations: run client-side first for immediate feedback, then server-side as final check. Classify results as 'warning' vs 'error'. Non-blocking warnings allow 'Approve anyway'.
ux-bot: Tip: provide a lightweight reason field (optional) in the bulk-approve modal and surface it in audit entries for traceability. Also suggest an 'Undo window' of 30s by default, configurable per org.
sam: perf note: lazy-load heavy threads when opening comment flyouts in large suites; show aria-busy during load.
maria: action items I'll take: 1) standardize header to 'Changes' + per-row 'Regression' badges, 2) rename bulk CTA to 'Approve runs' and split Run/Approve, 3) add pre-approve validation modal with warning/error flows, 4) tabbable toast undo with LIFO semantics and explicit counts, 5) compact comment dot + keyboard flyout, 6) density toggle with SR announcements, 7) Pilot approve presets + promote + audit + revert. I'll update Figma & spec and ping for final pass. :thumbsup:
